assertions.name: power_2_beats_power_1_and_3
assertions.source: n_q = 2 gives the smallest error among powers 1, 2, 3. This records a consistency check, NOT evidence for the exponent -- see data.squaring_proof.scope.

description: Derive m_K/m_π = χ_{(2,1)}(σ₁⁵) × (V_Seifert(T(2,5))/V_Seifert(T(2,3)))² = (q₀⁵ − q₀⁻⁵) × (9/5)² ≈ 3.536 (vs PDG 3.537, 290 ppm). The algebraic part is the Hecke character of the strange-quark braid on the standard (2,1) representation. The squaring reflects the 2-quark meson structure (one Seifert volume factor per constituent). SUPERSEDED for the accuracy dashboard: this (9/5)² form was formerly scored there and was withdrawn from that role. The canonical closure is [3]_q[4]_q + (α_em/π)(1 + log(1+ℏ_q)) (prop:meson-em-sinh-closed-form), at 51.5 ppb. This form's 290 ppm misses the observable's 263.6 ppb target by 1099x, so do NOT quote 290 ppm as the framework's accuracy on m_K/m_π.

hecke_characters.note: χ_{(2,1)}(σ₁ⁿ) = qⁿ + (−q⁻¹)ⁿ = qⁿ − q⁻ⁿ for odd n

squaring_proof.conclusion: Power = 2 (meson qq̄) gives 290 ppm; power = 1 gives 444605 ppm; power = 3 gives 799479 ppm.
squaring_proof.scope: This scan is a CONSISTENCY CHECK, not a derivation, and the key name `squaring_proof` overstates it. The two-body rationale names n_q = 2 in advance; the alternatives miss by 44% and 80% rather than marginally, so a scan that selected the exponent against the data would look no different. What it establishes is only that the a-priori exponent is not contradicted. Prior wording read 'The data selects n_q = 2', which is the fitted reading and is withdrawn (2026-08-22).
